newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Vietnam hails child drug informants.
newsitem.headline: Vietnam hails child drug informants.

text.p: Vietnam, awaiting the outcome of a sensational drugs trial, said on Wednesday an informant campaign among Hanoi schoolchildren had netted more than 170 drug-addicted students.
The daily Vietnam News said boxes for anonymous letters, posted at schools around the capital, had helped identify pushers, selling points and drug users.

"...Through the system, 173 students were denounced as being addicted to drugs, 81 drug-dealing points adjacent to schools were named, and three touts who urged students to use drugs were identified," the paper said.
But over-lenient punishments and ineffective school propaganda campaigns meant the problem of drug abuse among Vietnamese children was still increasing, it said.
Drugs experts have warned that Vietnam's children are being targeted by narcotics syndicates hoping to create a new market in one of the world's poorest countries.

"The problem did not exist a few years ago," said Rima Salah of the United Nations Childrens Fund in Hanoi. "The data is not very scientific but we're hearing reports that up to 50 percent of children in some schools are taking drugs."

Teachers at the Bach Dang school in northeastern Quang Ninh province told Reuters that the problem of food vendors plying drug-laced drinks and food on students had become so serious that the school had decided to build a 200-metre (656 ft) brick wall around the compound to keep pushers at bay.
"There are measures to prevent drugs and this is only one of them as we have to protect our pupils," school board member Nguyen Duc Dich said by phone.
Court verdicts in a dramatic drugs scandal involving some 22 people, including police and border officials, were expected to be announced on Wednesday following a widely publicised trial in Hanoi.
The prosecution has called for the death penalty for eight of the defendants.
